# Code of Conduct

## Our pledge

We are committed to providing a welcoming, professional, and harassment-free environment for everyone participating in Threat Claim Monitor, regardless of background, identity, experience level, or role.

## Expected behavior

- Communicate respectfully and assume good intent while reviewing evidence critically.
- Give actionable technical feedback focused on the work.
- Acknowledge uncertainty and correct mistakes transparently.
- Respect privacy, source restrictions, and responsible disclosure.
- Keep discussions relevant to defensive cybersecurity and the project scope.
- Help less experienced contributors understand decisions and tradeoffs.

## Unacceptable behavior

- Harassment, discrimination, intimidation, or personal attacks.
- Publishing another person’s private information without permission.
- Sharing stolen personal data, credentials, malware, or harmful payloads through project channels.
- Using the project to target, threaten, extort, or publicly accuse an organization.
- Publicly disclosing an unpatched vulnerability before coordinated handling.
- Repeatedly disrupting technical discussion or review.

## Security and victim sensitivity

Ransomware and breach claims may concern real victims. Contributors must avoid sensationalism and must not present unverified criminal claims as confirmed facts. Demonstrations use synthetic or redacted data.

## Reporting

Report conduct concerns privately to the repository owner. Security vulnerabilities follow `SECURITY.md`, not the conduct process.

## Enforcement

The maintainer may edit or remove contributions, comments, issues, or other participation that violates these expectations. Repeated or severe violations may result in temporary or permanent exclusion from project spaces.
